target_customer: Homelab and self-hosting users (free open source), plus IT teams and companies paying for hosted, hybrid or enterprise remote access
problem: Securely exposing and reaching private apps and infrastructure usually means proprietary tools such as Cloudflare Tunnels or Zscaler, or legacy VPNs with open inbound ports.
business_model: Open source core (AGPL-3 per most sources) with paid cloud, hybrid and enterprise editions; free starting tier
product_category: Open source zero trust networking, reverse proxy and remote access

founders.name: Milo Schwartz
founders.background_notes: Founding engineer on intelligent transportation and public works connectivity and monitoring systems; brother of Owen.

founders.name: Owen Schwartz
prior_employers: Smart mobility startup (founding engineer, four years)
founders.background_notes: Founding engineer on public works systems; the brothers worked together there.

competitors.name: Cloudflare Tunnels
competitors.what: Managed tunnel and access product, with only the cloudflared daemon open source
competitors.traction_then: Named as the main incumbent alternative in the YC launch post

competitors.name: Zscaler ZPA
competitors.traction_then: Named in the YC launch post

competitors.name: ngrok
competitors.traction_then: Named in the YC launch post

technical_complexity.rationale: A WireGuard based tunneled proxy with identity and access control is standard but broad engineering; it has grown to SSH, RDP, VNC, device posture and an AI gateway.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code can be forked, and rivals like Tailscale and Cloudflare are strong; its edge is community adoption and self-hosting.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or acquisition found yet; Pangolin's own comparison page frames Cloudflare's Access and WARP as proprietary.

market_need_then: Self-hosters and IT teams wanted an open source alternative to proprietary tunnels; the project reported about 12,600 GitHub stars and 140,000 installs about five months before the launch post.

branding.domain_note: Uses pangolin.net; also docs.digpangolin.com for docs. The exact pangolin.com was not obtained.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, developer oriented; a news post titled Pangolin v Cloudflare compares itself openly with the incumbent

branding.community_and_virality: Show HN post reached 484 points; active Discord (2,700+ members) and GitHub (15,000 stars) per YC; many third-party tutorials and blogs.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong open source grassroots pull in the self-hosting community, but the name is shared with a DEX, Pangolin.js and other projects.

pivots.from: Open source Cloudflare Tunnel alternative (self-hosted reverse proxy)
pivots.to: Broader secure access platform: business VPN, privileged access, AI gateway
pivots.why: Expansion shown by the YC tagline and website; stated reasons not found.

outcome_analysis: Pangolin grew bottom up as an open source Cloudflare Tunnels alternative, reaching about 15,000 GitHub stars, 315,000 deployments and 675 paying customers by the YC listing before its Summer 2025 batch concluded. It is active and has widened into business VPN and AI gateway features. Funding is unclear in public sources, and revenue is not verified, so the outcome is open.
notes: Funding unverified: StartupIntros lists a $500K seed (May 2025), VCBacked lists $4.7M total with a seed announced October 2025 and investors 468 Capital, Y Combinator, Chemistry and Pioneer Fund; the company's own seed round post could not be fetched (404). None recorded as rounds. Traction numbers (stars, customers) are from the YC listing and company claims. Competitors come from the YC launch post of 2025 and are not independently dated. Licence listed as AGPL-3 by most sources and GPL-3.0 by one. Completeness pass: two seed entries recorded, each from a single database. StartupIntros gives $500K dated 2025-05 with no investors; VCBacked gives a seed dated October 2025 with a $4.7M company total and no per-round amount. They may describe the same or different rounds. A Linuxiac article confirms a recent seed round but gives no amount or date.
